<title>President of Harvard University</title>
<fragment>

Recently, however, the job has become increasingly administrative, especially as fund-raising campaigns have taken on central importance in large institutions such as Harvard. Some have criticized this trend to the extent it has prevented the president from focusing on substantive issues in higher education.[3]


Each president is professor in some department of the university and teaches from time to time.


Harvard's current president is Claudine Gay, having become Harvard's 30th president on July 1, 2023.[4]


She succeeded Lawrence Bacow who retired on June 30, 2023.[5]




## History[edit]


At Harvard's founding it was headed by a "schoolmaster," Nathaniel Eaton. In 1640, when Henry Dunster was brought in, he adopted the title president. The origins of this title have been grounds for a certain amount of speculation.


Harvard was founded for the training of Puritan clergy, and even though its mission was soon broadened, nearly all presidents through the end of the 18th century were in holy orders.


</fragment>
<fragment>

All presidents from Leonard Hoar through Nathan Pusey were graduates of Harvard College. Of the presidents since Pusey, Bok earned his undergraduate degree at Stanford, Rudenstine at Princeton, and Summers and Bacow at MIT, but each earned a graduate degree at Harvard. Drew Gilpin Faust was the first president since the seventeenth century with no earned Harvard degree.


John Winthrop served as acting president in 1769 and again in 1773; but both times he declined an offer of the full presidency on grounds of old age.


</fragment>

Harvard is a famously decentralized university, noted for the "every tub on its own bottom" independence of its various constituent faculties. They set their own academic standards and manage their own budgets. The president, however, plays an important part in university-wide planning and strategy. Each names a faculty's dean (and, since the foundation of the office in 1994, the university's provost), and grants tenure to recommended professors; however, the president is expected to make such decisions after extensive consultation with faculty members.


Harvard presidents have traditionally influenced educational practices nationwide. Charles W. Eliot, for example, originated America's familiar system of a smorgasbord of elective courses available to each student;[2] James B. content:
**Peter Salovey** (born February 21, 1958) is an American psychologist, academic administrator, and the 23rd President of Yale University (2013‑2024). He is best known for co‑founding the field of **emotional intelligence** with John D. Mayer, and for his extensive research on social and personality psychology, especially the ways emotions influence cognition, judgment, and interpersonal behavior. --- ### Key Points | Category | Details | |----------|---------| | **Current Role** | President of Yale University (2013‑2024). Succeeded Rick Levin and was succeeded by **Michael McInnis** in 2024. | | **Academic Background** | • B.A. in Psychology, Stanford University (1979)
• M.A. and Ph.D. in Psychology, University of Michigan (1983) | | **Research Focus** | • Emotional intelligence (EI) – development of the Mayer‑Salovey model
• Social cognition, self‑regulation, and interpersonal processes
• Applications of EI to education, health, and leadership | | **Major Publications** | • *The Emotional Intelligence of Leaders* (1997)
• *Emotional Intelligence: New Ability or Eclectic Traits?* (1997)
• *The Psychology of Emotional Intelligence* (1999) (co‑edited) | | **Awards & Honors** | • Fellow of the American Academy of Arts & Sciences (2005)
• Member of the National Academy of Sciences (2020)
• Honorary Doctor of Humane Letters, National Tsing‑Hua University (2014) | | **Administrative Experience** | • Dean of Yale College (2005‑2009)
• Provost of Yale University (2009‑2013)
• President of Yale University (2013‑2024) | | **Public Service** | • Served on the board of the American Psychological Association
• Advisor to the U.S. Department of Education on emotional learning initiatives | | **Personal** | Married to **Laura K. Salovey**, a professor of linguistics; they have two children. | --- ### Why He’s Notable 1. **Emotional Intelligence Pioneer** – Salovey’s work with John D. Mayer introduced a scientifically grounded model of EI, framing it as a set of abilities (perceiving, using, understanding, and managing emotions) rather than a collection of personality traits. This model has become the foundation for decades of research, assessment tools, and educational programs worldwide. 2. **Yale Leadership** – As Yale’s president, Salovey oversaw major initiatives: the expansion of undergraduate financial aid, the launch of the **Yale Center for Emotional Intelligence**, campus sustainability projects, and the modernization of the university’s residential system. He also guided Yale through the COVID‑19 pandemic, implementing hybrid learning and health‑safety protocols. 3. **Interdisciplinary Impact** – Salovey’s research bridges psychology, education, health, and business. His EI framework is applied in corporate leadership training, school curricula, clinical interventions, and public‑policy design. --- ### Quick Bio Timeline | Year | Milestone | |------|-----------| | **1979** | B.A., Stanford University (Psychology) | | **1983** | Ph.D., University of Michigan (Psychology) | | **1985‑1994** | Faculty, University of Michigan (Assistant → Associate Professor) | | **1995‑2005** | Professor of Psychology, Yale University | | **1995** | Publishes seminal paper on emotional intelligence with John Mayer | | **2005‑2009** | Dean of Yale College | | **2009‑2013** | Provost, Yale University | | **2013‑2024** | President, Yale University | | **2020** | Elected to the National Academy of Sciences | | **2024** | Steps down; succeeded by Michael McInnis | --- ### Further Reading & Resources - **Wikipedia:** “Peter Salovey” – comprehensive overview of his life, research, and presidency. - **Yale University Biography:** Official page with his statements, speeches, and initiatives. - **Mayer‑Salovey Model of Emotional Intelligence:** Scholarly articles and the *Emotion Review* journal special issues. - **Books:** *The Emotional Intelligence of Leaders* (Harvard Business Review Press) – a concise guide to applying EI in organizational settings. If you’d like more detail on any specific aspect—his research contributions, Yale initiatives, or a list of his major publications—just let me know!
